name: Tyrannosaurus rex
found_regions: Western North America (Hell Creek Formation, Montana/Dakotas/Wyoming)
notes: Lived in subtropical-to-warm-temperate floodplains and coastal forests with distinct wet/dry seasons.
sources: Arens & Allen (2014), 'A florule from the base of the Hell Creek Formation...': leaf-margin MAT ~7-11C (CLAMP 11-12C +/-2C), leaf-area MAP ~1910-1970mm.
Wikipedia, 'Hell Creek Formation': mild subtropical/temperate climate, no prolonged freeze, based on crocodilian and palm fossils.

name: Triceratops horridus
notes: Grazed open floodplains near rivers; same formation and climate envelope as T. rex, its known contemporary and predator.
sources: Arens & Allen (2014), Hell Creek Formation florule study, as above.
Co-occurrence data: Triceratops and T. rex are recovered from the same Hell Creek Formation localities.

name: Velociraptor mongoliensis
found_regions: Central Asia (Djadochta Formation, Gobi Desert, Mongolia)
notes: Adapted to an arid eolian dune environment with interdune oases and seasonal sandstorms. Multiple sources note the present-day Gobi Desert climate at Djadochta sites differs little from 80 Mya, aside from being somewhat warmer and less arid then, an unusually direct modern-paleo analog.
sources: Wikipedia / Fossil Wiki, 'Djadochta Formation': arid habitat of sand dunes, little freshwater apart from oases and arroyos; present-day climate at most sites differs little from ~80 Mya.
Grokipedia, 'Djadochta Formation': eolian dune sands, interdune ponds/lakes, semiarid depositional conditions.

name: Stegosaurus stenops
notes: Semiarid floodplains with strong wet-dry seasonality, open woodland and fern prairies; high atmospheric CO2 implied warm temperatures.
sources: Retallack (1997), cited in ScienceDirect summary 'The implications of a dry climate...': Morrison paleosols indicate MAP of only 600-900mm with a dry season.
Demko & Parrish (1998): GCM results predict a rain-shadow effect creating semiarid to arid conditions over the Morrison basin.

name: Brachiosaurus altithorax
notes: Browsed tall conifers in warm semiarid-to-subhumid floodplain woodlands; MAP estimates vary regionally within the Morrison basin (drier south, wetter north).
sources: Myers et al., cited in SMU research news: geochemical MAP estimates ~45in (Montana) to ~20in (Wyoming) to ~30in (New Mexico) across the Morrison basin.

name: Spinosaurus aegyptiacus
notes: Semi-aquatic predator in a tropical coastal wetland system dominated by mangroves, lagoons, tidal flats, and river deltas; monsoonal, largely aseasonal warmth.
sources: Fandom/Surviving Earth, Spinosaurus paleoecology summary: tropical climate lacking defined seasons, violent monsoons, coastal wetland dominated by mangroves.
El Atfy et al. (2023-2025), Swiss Journal of Palaeontology, Bahariya Formation macroflora study: warm and humid paleoclimate disrupted by dry phases.

name: Ankylosaurus magniventris
notes: Same formation and climate envelope as T. rex and Triceratops; coastal floodplains and conifer forests.
sources: Arens & Allen (2014), Hell Creek Formation florule study, as above.

name: Parasaurolophus walkeri
found_regions: Western North America (Dinosaur Park Formation, Alberta)
notes: Humid coastal lowlands and river deltas along the Western Interior Seaway with dense vegetation. NOTE: this range is a formation-level qualitative interpretation (coastal floodplain deposits), not yet cross-checked against a quantitative multi-proxy study the way Hell Creek and Morrison were.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Dinosaur Park Formation': deposited on a coastal floodplain of the Western Interior Seaway, subtropical/warm-temperate, humid.

name: Allosaurus fragilis
notes: Apex predator of the same semiarid Morrison floodplain woodlands as Stegosaurus and Diplodocus, its known prey.
sources: Retallack (1997) / Demko & Parrish (1998), Morrison Formation paleoclimate, as above.

name: Iguanodon bernissartensis
notes: Warm-temperate floodplains and conifer-fern forests with mild, wet winters. NOTE: formation-level qualitative interpretation, not a quantitative multi-proxy reconstruction.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Wealden Group': freshwater and floodplain deposits, warm temperate climate interpretation based on sedimentology and flora.

name: Diplodocus carnegii
notes: Grazed low ground vegetation across the same semiarid Morrison floodplains as Stegosaurus and Allosaurus.
sources: Retallack (1997) / Demko & Parrish (1998), Morrison Formation paleoclimate, as above.

name: Argentinosaurus huinculensis
notes: Semiarid to sub-humid inland fluvial plains. NOTE: formation-level qualitative interpretation, not a quantitative multi-proxy reconstruction.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Candeleros Formation': fluvial and eolian deposits interpreted as a semiarid inland environment.
